name: org.machanism.machai:mcp-server-maven-plugin
description: MCP Server Maven Plugin is a Java 17 Maven plugin that starts a Machai Model Context Protocol (MCP) server as part of a Maven build. It exposes configured Machai AI tools over HTTP without a separate server launcher, supporting local development, integration testing, demonstrations, and build-driven AI workflows. Its aggregator goals, stateless and streamable, respectively start stateless HTTP and streamable HTTP MCP server transports using the current Maven project name, version, and base directory. Both goals load the configured PropertiesConfigurator, configure the HTTP port and project directory, register configured tools, and apply configured parameter values as JVM system properties without replacing values already supplied to the process. Maven execution errors report configuration and startup failures. As aggregator goals, they support reactor builds by starting one server representing the multi-module build. The registered stop_mcp_server function initiates an orderly delayed JVM shutdown after an MCP client completes its work.

constructors.description: Creates the lifecycle function-tools component that exposes the MCP server shutdown operation to a running Machai MCP server.

examples.description: For an embedded Java integration, create the lifecycle tool and request a normal shutdown. In usual plugin use, the MCP server registers this tool from its configuration rather than application code creating it directly.

features.name: stateless
features.description: Starts a stateless HTTP MCP server as an aggregator Maven goal. It applies configured parameters, initializes the server from Maven project metadata and the MCP configuration file, sets the project directory and HTTP port, registers configured tools, and starts the endpoint.

examples.description: Step 1: add this plugin to the consuming Maven build, allowing Maven to resolve the ready-to-use component. Step 2: prepare the MCP properties file with Machai server and tool settings. Step 3: invoke the stateless goal with the port and configuration location, then connect an MCP-compatible HTTP client while Maven remains running.

features.name: streamable
features.description: Starts a streamable HTTP MCP server as an aggregator Maven goal. It uses the same Maven project metadata, configuration, parameter, base-directory, port, and tool-registration handling as stateless, but selects the streamable HTTP transport.

examples.description: Step 1: resolve the plugin by invoking its fully specified Maven coordinates. Step 2: supply a readable Machai MCP configuration with mcp.config and an available port with mcp.port. Step 3: run the streamable goal and configure the MCP client for the resulting streamable HTTP endpoint.

features.name: stopMcpServer
features.description: Initiates an orderly delayed MCP server shutdown, logs the shutdown event, and exits the JVM with the supplied exit code. The default MCP function argument is 0, indicating normal completion. This function tool is supported for McpServer.

examples.description: After an MCP client completes a local development or test workflow, invoke the registered stop_mcp_server function with exit_code 0. The server returns an acknowledgement, waits briefly for the response to complete, and terminates normally.

customizations.name: mcp.config
customizations.description: Maven property identifying the readable MCP server configuration file used to load server and tool settings. Supply it for server startup.

examples.description: Pass the configuration file location at invocation time to keep environment-specific settings outside the project POM.

customizations.name: params
customizations.description: Optional map of values copied to JVM system properties only when the property has not already been provided.

examples.title: Run a local stateless MCP endpoint
steps: Add org.machanism.machai:mcp-server-maven-plugin:1.4.0-SNAPSHOT to the Maven build, or invoke it directly by Maven coordinates.
Prepare an mcp.properties file containing Machai MCP server and tool configuration.
Connect an MCP-compatible HTTP client to the configured endpoint and use its registered tools.
When the workflow is complete, invoke stop_mcp_server with exit_code 0 for orderly shutdown.
